title: Feladatok a munkahelyen: Accusative Objects at Work

sections.title: New verbs, the accusative you already know
sections.content: A workday is full of feladat ("task") after feladat, and describing them just means putting the accusative -t you already know onto the thing being done: jelentést ír ("writes a report"), e-mailt küld ("sends an email"), megbeszélést tart ("holds a meeting"). ír, küld and tart are new verbs, but the -t on jelentés, e-mail and megbeszélés works exactly like every other accusative object you've built.

items.spanish: Ma egy jelentést írok, és két e-mailt küldök.
items.english: Today I'm writing a report, and sending two emails.
Petra is holding a meeting in the afternoon.

items.spanish: Egy új projekten dolgozunk a csapatommal.
items.english: We're working on a new project with my team.

sections.content: egy projekten dolgozik takes -on/-en/-ön, not the accusative — you're working "on" the project the same way you'd be "on" a surface, not acting on it directly the way you act on a jelentés you write.
